title: Constrained Auto-Bidding via Generative Response Modeling

problem.claim: Auto-bidding must maximize advertiser value over long horizons while satisfying budget and ratio constraints under non-stationary, uncertain traffic and auction dynamics.

gap.claim: Existing pacing, reinforcement-learning, and generative approaches either cannot anticipate future conditions or obscure constraint violations and degrade under distribution shift.

contributions.claim: The Generative Response Model predicts future traffic volume and horizon-aggregate cost/value curves conditioned on history and a single bid multiplier.
Under mild monotonicity assumptions, the optimality gap versus full per-tick control is bounded by the spread of per-tick marginal value-to-cost ratios.

A lightweight analytic controller enforces active constraints through one-dimensional root finding and is exact for the single-multiplier problem, with receding-horizon violations bounded by prediction error.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On AuctionNet, the authors report improved constraint stability and overall score compared with existing baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Long-horizon constrained auto-bidding operates under uncertain and changing traffic and auction conditions.
Prior control, reinforcement-learning, and generative approaches have limitations in anticipating conditions or preserving constraints under distribution shift.
GRM models future responses as functions of a single bid multiplier.
The paper provides an optimality-gap bound and an analytic constraint controller with exactness and violation guarantees.
Experiments on AuctionNet report better constraint stability and overall score than existing baselines.

source_observation.claim: The method predicts aggregate responses to a single bid multiplier and then uses analytic control to enforce constraints.

interpretation.claim: Separating response modeling from constraint control may make constraint handling more explicit and analyzable.

application.claim: In other sequential decision systems, model how outcomes respond to a compact control variable before applying a dedicated constraint solver.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this decomposition works beyond the stated monotonicity assumptions, single-multiplier setting, or prediction-error regime.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical effect sizes beyond naming AuctionNet and reporting improvement.
The abstract does not provide details of the monotonicity conditions, prediction-error bounds, or implementation.
